definition: Hapless means dogged by misfortune through no fault of your own — bad luck that just keeps arriving.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word hapless. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know hapless should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The hapless street magician drew his first real crowd just as a gust scattered his cards into the fountain.
Unlucky is milder than hapless — one bad break is unlucky; hapless suggests misfortune has adopted you.
Doomed goes further than hapless — a hapless traveler misses the train, while a doomed venture is certain to end in disaster.

Luckless states the bare fact of bad luck, flat and dry — a luckless gambler, a luckless season — without the note of pity hapless carries. Where hapless smiles kindly at misfortune's favorite target, luckless just records that fortune never showed up.

Jinxed blames a cause: some curse or bad charm seems to make things go wrong, and people say it half-seriously. Hapless points to no cause at all — misfortune simply keeps choosing the same blameless person, which is why hapless carries pity instead of superstition.

Every food-truck owner has bad days; Tomas has a collection.
In one summer his generator failed during the festival rush, a parade rerouted straight through his best corner, and a health inspector arrived minutes after a seagull did.
None of it was carelessness.
His logs were clean, his permits current, his fryer spotless — the trouble simply kept finding him.
Regulars started calling him their hapless hero, saying it with real affection, and lining up on his worst days out of loyalty.
Tomas keeps a photo of the seagull taped to the register.
If misfortune insists on choosing him, he says, it can at least pay for a sandwich.
